visual_goal: Show the decade view: products, providers and actors on the left change on external timetables and connect to a small durable core the enterprise owns, which it keeps in its own form.
prompt: A left-to-right illustration in two halves. The left half is a busy, shifting area with small swirling motion lines and a few small clock icons, labeled at its top 'Volatile'. In it, five rounded boxes stacked vertically, each slightly tilted as if drifting, top to bottom: 'PSPs and banks', 'ERP products', 'Tax engines', 'Brands and markets', 'People and agents'. The right half is a calm, solid stone keep labeled at its top 'Durable core'. Inside the keep, a left column of three blocks: at the top, level with 'PSPs and banks', a small block 'Owned identifiers' with a key icon; in the middle a tall orange block 'Canonical events' with a lightning bolt, spanning the height of 'ERP products', 'Tax engines' and 'Brands and markets'; at the bottom, level with 'People and agents', a block 'Evidence store' with a filing cabinet. In a right column, at middle height, a block 'Books of record' with an open ledger. All arrows from the left are straight and horizontal: 'PSPs and banks' into 'Owned identifiers'; 'ERP products', 'Tax engines' and 'Brands and markets' each into the tall 'Canonical events' block; 'People and agents' into 'Evidence store'. Inside the keep: one arrow from 'Canonical events' right into 'Books of record', and one arrow from 'Books of record' down-left into 'Evidence store'. Exactly seven arrows.
alt: On the left, drifting boxes for ERP products, PSPs and banks, tax engines, brands and markets, and people and agents; on the right, a stone keep holding owned identifiers, canonical events, books of record and an evidence store; the volatile parts connect into the core, and events derive the books, which are proved with evidence.

visual_goal: Show the stressor-analysis loop: each stressor is simulated and the design changed until the residue is acceptable, changes are recorded, the incidence matrix shows which changes recur, those become residues built into the roadmap, and fresh stressors test them the next year.
prompt: A left-to-right illustration. At the far left, a small building labeled 'Estate as is', with one arrow right into the inner loop. The inner loop sits left of center: four stations on a circle. On the left of the circle 'Pick a stressor' with a lightning bolt (this is the station the arrow from 'Estate as is' enters); at the top of the circle 'Simulate' with a wind tunnel icon; on the right of the circle 'Change design' with a pencil on a blueprint; at the bottom of the circle 'Record' with a notebook. Clockwise arrows on the circle: 'Pick a stressor' into 'Simulate'; 'Simulate' into 'Change design'; 'Change design' into 'Record'; and one arrow labeled 'next stressor' from 'Record' into 'Pick a stressor'. One straight vertical shortcut arrow through the middle of the circle from 'Simulate' down into 'Record'. To the right of the loop, in one row at the height of 'Record': a large highlighted grid with a few columns filled in more densely than the rest, labeled 'Incidence matrix', then a single brick wall section labeled 'Build residues', then a calendar page with lightning bolts labeled 'Fresh stressors'. One arrow from 'Record' right into 'Incidence matrix', one from the matrix into 'Build residues', one from 'Build residues' into 'Fresh stressors'. One long arching arrow over the top of the whole picture from 'Fresh stressors' back to 'Estate as is'. Exactly ten arrows.
alt: An inner loop picks a stressor, simulates it, changes the design if needed and records the change, then repeats; the records feed an incidence matrix whose recurring changes are built as residues, tested against fresh stressors, and fed back to the estate.

visual_goal: Show the annual rhythm as a cycle where each review feeds the next, and the stressor review closes the loop by ranking residues before the strategy refresh re-baselines the roadmap.
prompt: A large circular year wheel drawn as a ring track, with four stations placed around it clockwise: at the top 'Strategy refresh' with a small tag 'March'; at the right 'Portfolio review' with a small tag 'June'; at the bottom 'Vendor review' with a small tag 'September'; at the left a highlighted station 'Stressor review' with a small tag 'Nov to Dec'. In the center of the wheel a small gauge icon labeled 'Fitness reviews' with a tiny tag 'quarterly'. Ring arrows going clockwise: 'Strategy refresh' into 'Portfolio review', 'Portfolio review' into 'Vendor review', 'Vendor review' into 'Stressor review' labeled 'vendor events', and a thick orange arrow from 'Stressor review' into 'Strategy refresh' labeled 'residue ranking'. Inside the wheel: one arrow from 'Strategy refresh' into 'Fitness reviews', one arrow from 'Fitness reviews' into 'Portfolio review', one dashed arrow from 'Fitness reviews' into 'Stressor review' labeled 'breaches'. One dashed arrow back from 'Stressor review' into 'Vendor review' labeled 'new stressors'. Exactly eight arrows.
alt: A year wheel: March strategy refresh, quarterly fitness reviews, June portfolio review, September vendor review and November to December stressor review, which feeds residue ranking back into the strategy refresh; fitness breaches and vendor events feed the stressor review, which returns new stressors to the vendor review.
